title: Listening Comprehension
intro: Listen to a dialogue, then answer multiple choice questions. These are generated review dialogues because the final exam dialogue is not provided in advance.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Our health poster needs a main idea and three supporting details.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: How about this main idea: A balanced lunch helps students learn and play.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Good. We can support it with fruit, vegetables, whole grains, and water.

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: Should we add a picture of a lunch tray with labels?

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Yes, the labels will help younger students understand the food groups.

questions.q: What are Mina and Owen making?
What main idea does Owen suggest?
choices: A balanced lunch helps students learn and play.
Water should never be part of lunch.
A lunch tray needs no labels.

questions.q: Which detail supports the main idea?
Why do they want labels on the picture?
choices: To help younger students understand the food groups
To make the poster harder to read

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Tomorrow each group will explain one eco-friendly choice.

lines.speaker: Jay
lines.text: Our group wants to explain why reusable containers are better than throwaway bags.

lines.speaker: Jay
lines.text: Families at the school fair. We want them to pack snacks with less waste.

lines.speaker: Teacher
lines.text: Then use clear examples and a chart that compares the two choices.

questions.q: What topic will Jay's group explain?
What does the teacher suggest adding?
choices: A chart that compares two choices
A list of spelling words only
To persuade families to pack snacks with less waste
To entertain people with a tall tale
To ask for a new notebook
